newsitem.title: UK: Ingersoll Rand offers to buy Britain's Newman Tonks.
newsitem.headline: Ingersoll Rand offers to buy Britain's Newman Tonks.

text.p: Ingersoll-Rand Co. Monday launched a surprise cash offer for British building products group Newman Tonks Group valuing the company at around 230 million pounds ($376 million).
Ingersoll's offer sidelined a hostile bid from British engineering group FKI Plc, which had valued Newman at 195.7 million pounds ($320 million).
Newman's board had rejected FKI's offer but gave its unanimous backing to Ingersoll's bid, saying it represented a 28 percent premium over the FKI's "unsolicited and hostile offer."

The offer by Woodcliff Lakes, N.J.-based Ingersoll, a multinational manufacturer of industrial machinery, was welcomed by investors, and Newman shares surged 28 pence, or 18.5 percent, to 179-1/2 pence.
Newman directors have already accepted the Ingersoll offer in respect of 1.2 million shares representing 0.9 percent of the issued share capital.
Ingersoll-Rand vice president Brian Jellison said Newman Tonks would help the architectural hardware group to shape its European strategy.
"It will serve us better in the fast-growing Asian markets as well," Jellison said.
Newman's exports, both direct and indirect, account for almost 20 percent of its total revenues.
Newman also forecast profits before tax, exceptional items and bid costs of not less than 18 million pounds ($29.4 million) for the year to Dec. 31, 1996.
Newman's 1995 pretax profit was 27.2 million pounds ($44.5 million).
Jellison did not make a commitment to retain all of Newman's 4,500 employees but said the acquisition would "see job creations."
Jellison said the group was to announce its 1996 results on Monday and was expecting a 15 percent growth, its average for the last three years.
Separately, FKI said it had acceptances for its offer of some 20.6 percent of Newman Tonks shares, and said it owned or had agreed to buy further shares totalling 0.4 percent.

FKI's offer, which was scheduled to close on Feb. 7, had been accepted by fund management groups M&G and Britannic Assurance, who control some 13.37 percent of Newman Tonks shares. None was immediately available for comment.
